text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. .
-- The government announced new rates for Malaysia's privately owned utility, Indah Water Konsortium's water and sewerage services. .

- Telekom Malaysia Bhd is to reduce its charges for Integrated Service Digital Network (ISDN) calls by one third from January. The new rates for data transmission will be in line with charges for standard voice calls.

- IOI Corporation Bhd plans to list its industrial gas producing subsidiary on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's (KLSE) second board by the middle of 1997 to raise funds for the unit's expansion plans. The company is also planning to build a new township in Selangor state. .

- Sungei Way Condstruction Bhd has received the approval of the Securities Commission to the listed on the KLSE's main board. The flotation exercise will involve the public issue of 48 million new shares. .

- Lingkaran Trans Kota Holdings Bhd (Litrak), scheduled to be listed on the KLSE main board on December 16, will impose toll charges on the 40km highway it is building near Kuala Lumpur, beginning in 1998.

- Transwater Corporation Bhd and France-based Lyonnaise are to forge an "alliance" for future joint ventures in Malaysia, executives from the two companies said on Thursday. The companies will participate in water treatment projects in Malaysia, they said.
